title: AI-rewrite: deliberation doc schema
description: Strict schema for AI-rewrite output of deliberation/discussion docs. Strict-core, open-extensions: every object has a closed key set; doc-specific structure goes under an optional `extensions:` key on each object. The closed core covers: items → options → pros/cons/verdict → lean → open_questions, plus optional cross-cutting interaction and ordering blocks.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the source. 'deliberation' = still open; 'spec-ready' = lean is defensible, ready for /spec; 'spec' = a requirements doc has been derived; 'shipped' = implementation merged; 'rejected' = abandoned; 'archived' = historical only.

sibling_human.description: Path to the human-prose source doc.

sibling_lossless.description: Path to a lossless variant if one exists.

refs.description: Slug → path map. Reference as e.g. 'refs.spec' in body strings.

glossary.description: Term → definition map. Define repeated terms / acronyms / id schemes once.

trigger.description: Concrete observation / incident / question that prompted the deliberation. Quote real numbers, paths, identifiers when available.

items.description: Map of item-key → item. A deliberation may co-locate multiple items if they surfaced from the same observation; otherwise typically one item.

interaction.description: Cross-cutting concerns when the deliberation has multiple items. Omit if there's only one item.

ordering.description: Release / sequencing notes for the items. Omit if not yet decided.

extensions.description: Top-level escape hatch for doc-specific structure that doesn't fit the closed core.

name.description: Short kebab-case slug for the item (e.g. 'introspection-via-direct-neo4j').

problem.description: What's wrong / unaddressed / open. Concrete, not abstract.

today_behavior.description: Optional list of how the system currently behaves in the relevant area. Useful when the problem is 'this works but is broken / incomplete', not 'this doesn't exist'.

options.description: Map of option-key → option. Option keys are short and convention-aligned (e.g. '1a', '1b', '2a'). Minimum 2 options — a one-option deliberation isn't really a deliberation.

lean.description: The recommended option (or composition of options). Omit only if the item is genuinely unresolved.

shapes.description: Optional map of shape-key → shape, when the lean is a composition of multiple options rather than a single pick (e.g. 'Shape A = 2c + 2d').

decision_gate.description: Optional. The criterion that distinguishes which shape / option to pick when the lean is conditional.

open_questions.description: Questions that need answering before the item becomes a spec. Distinguish 'blocks the lean' from 'spec-time decision' via the open_question structure.

extensions.description: Item-level escape hatch for doc-specific structure.

name.description: Short kebab-case slug describing the option (e.g. 'document-pattern-in-SKILL.md').

action.description: What this option does, concretely. Includes file paths, command shapes, schema changes — enough to picture the implementation.

pros.description: Honest upsides. A pros-only or pros-empty option list is a failure mode.

cons.description: Honest downsides. Either a flat string list (simple options) or a map of named-issue → details (when the option has structured / categorized cons that benefit from named anchors).

verdict.description: rejected = ruled out; accepted = part of the lean; tentative = leaning toward but not decided; pending = no judgment yet.

verdict_reason.description: One-line rationale for the verdict. Especially important for 'rejected' — preserve the reasoning trail.

code_sketch.description: Generic code snippet illustrating the option.

cypher_sketch.description: Cypher snippet (use this instead of code_sketch when the option is a graph query).

pick.description: The option-key (or shape-key, or composition) being recommended. Free-form string because composite picks like 'A (start with), 2e queued' don't fit a single key.

because.description: Defensible reasoning for the pick. Not 'it depends' — the criteria you'd defend in review.

landing.description: Concrete steps for how the lean would be executed. Mixed-type items allowed (strings or nested maps).

rationale.description: Optional longer rationale when 'because' isn't enough.

synergy_note.description: Optional note on how this lean interacts with adjacent work (other items, prior releases, ongoing initiatives).

name.description: Short label for the shape (e.g. 'prevent + warn').

composition.description: Which options compose this shape (e.g. '2c + 2d' or '2c + 2d + 2e').

intent.description: What this shape is trying to achieve, in one line.

requires.description: Prerequisites or dependencies the shape pulls in.

q.description: The question, phrased as a question.

answer.description: Resolved answer. Use this only when the deliberation has actually settled the question.

likely.description: Tentative answer with reasoning. Distinct from 'answer' to flag that this is the agent's lean, not a settled call.

belongs_to.description: Where this question gets resolved (e.g. '2d behavior spec', 'spec-time decision', 'blocks the lean').

conflict.description: Do the items conflict? 'none' = independent; 'minor' = adjacent / touch the same files; 'blocking' = picking one constrains the other.

synergy.description: How the items make each other better when shipped together.

ordering.description: Map of item-key → ordering notes, plus optional top-level constraints. Loose object because ordering shapes vary widely.
